clue.text: Dry pulp for fuel housed in military camp

indicators.note: something housed in a place sits within its walls, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: a base is where troops are stationed
gas is a fuel burned for heat

explanation.surface: Fuel made from dried pulp is stored at an army camp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dry pulp for fuel' reads as one phrase, but the definition stops at 'pulp'; 'for' joins it to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Bagasse is the fibrous residue left after crushing sugar cane, often burned as fuel.

clue.text: For part of dress person needs diamonds

parts.note: bod is informal British for a person
ice is slang for diamonds

explanation.surface: Someone making a dress needs diamonds for one part of it.
explanation.walkthrough: Ice is underworld slang for diamonds; a bod is a British colloquial word for a person.
explanation.definitionFit: A bodice is the upper section of a woman's dress, fitting the torso.

clue.text: Chief invader's artistic style

parts.note: the Goths were a Germanic people who invaded the Roman Empire
i/c stands for 'in charge', so someone chief

explanation.surface: The leader of an invading horde has a particular artistic style.
explanation.walkthrough: The two pieces appear in the reverse order of the clue: the invader comes first and the chief follows; the 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Gothic names a medieval style of architecture and art with pointed arches and soaring vaults.

clue.text: What can make men sick: ale fomented with sweet food

indicators.note: fomented means stirred up, so these letters are agitated into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A warning that stirred-up ale taken with sweets can make men ill.
explanation.walkthrough: A simnel cake is a British fruit cake with marzipan, traditionally eaten at Easter or on Mothering Sunday.
explanation.definitionFit: This traditional rich fruit cake topped with marzipan is a sweet thing to eat.

clue.text: The Continental fashion suits British singer

parts.note: el is 'the' in Spanish, a Continental language
ton is an old word for fashion or high style

explanation.surface: European fashion looks good on a British pop star.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Continental' means 'the' in a European language; Spanish el is the one wanted here.
explanation.definitionFit: Elton John is a celebrated English singer and pianist, known by his first name.

clue.text: Inventor whose produce may be diverse

indicators.note: what the answer may produce is a rearranged version of its own letters, so the clue word is the result, not the source

parts.note: the clue gives the rearranged form; work back to find the original

explanation.surface: An inventor's output is likely to be varied.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a reverse anagram: the answer's letters, rearranged, produce the word printed in the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who devises things contrives or invents them, so a deviser is an inventor.

clue.text: Something mucky on a Welshman's overalls

parts.note: dung is animal muck
taken as written
Rees is a common Welsh surname

explanation.surface: There is muck all over a Welshman's work clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Dungarees are hard-wearing trousers with a bib and straps, worn as protective workwear.

clue.text: Prohibition couched in negative tones

indicators.note: couched in means lying inside, so the letters sit within the following words

parts.note: the letters run across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: A ban is delivered in a disapproving tone of voice.
explanation.definitionFit: A veto is an authoritative refusal or ban on a proposed action.

clue.text: Of little significance? Editor is insulted!

parts.note: slight means minor or unimportant
ED is the standard abbreviation for editor

explanation.surface: An editor is offended at being told his work hardly matters.
explanation.definitionFit: To be slighted is to be snubbed or treated with disrespect, an insult.

clue.text: Man, one police trace finally — wanted for killing

parts.note: Reg is a man's name
the Roman numeral for one
CID is the Criminal Investigation Department of British police

indicators.note: finally points to the end of the word it follows, keeping only its closing letter

parts.note: the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A man wanted for murder is being traced by the police.
explanation.walkthrough: The CID is the plain-clothes detective branch of British police forces.
explanation.definitionFit: Regicide is the killing of a king, a specific kind of killing.

clue.text: Barrier will restrict union — that's a fact

indicators.note: to restrict is to hem in, so one word closes around the other

parts.note: a dam is a barrier holding back water
TU is the abbreviation for trade union

explanation.surface: A dispute where a blockade will hold back a trade union.
explanation.definitionFit: A datum is a single piece of information or given fact, the singular of data.

clue.text: See 15
"Armed conflict is shameful act" — Sadat

parts.note: a crime is a shameful or wrongful act
Anwar Sadat was President of Egypt

explanation.surface: An Egyptian president denounces war as a disgrace.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface quotes Sadat, but his first name is the second piece.
explanation.definitionFit: The Crimean War of 1853 to 1856 pitted Russia against Britain, France and Turkey.

clue.text: Young woman for the most part elegant

indicators.note: for the most part means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: chick is slang for a young woman

explanation.surface: A girl who is stylish most of the time.
explanation.definitionFit: Chic describes something stylish and fashionable, which is what elegant suggests.

clue.text: Art form with which you might see old lady fool the academy

parts.note: gran is an informal word for grandmother
a dope is a stupid person
RA is the Royal Academy of Arts in London

explanation.surface: An old woman makes fools of the art establishment.
explanation.definitionFit: Grand opera is a serious, fully sung operatic genre, a major form of musical art.

clue.text: Finishes without father, one real buddy

indicators.note: without in its old sense means outside, so the finishes wrap around what follows

parts.note: two words for finishes: close and end
F is the abbreviation for father
R abbreviates the real, a currency of Brazil and formerly Spain
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone who finishes things without a father has one true pal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finishes' supplies two synonyms that go either side of the middle letters; 'one' and 'real' appear in the answer in the reverse order of the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A close friend is an intimate companion, someone a person trusts as a mate or pal.

clue.text: Ann, too upset, going round concealing love object in a hopeless situation

indicators.note: going round means encircling, so the jumbled letters wrap around the next piece
upset means knocked over, so the name and the next word are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written, ready for jumbling
concealing is hiding
love is zero in tennis, which looks like O
a thing is an object

explanation.surface: Ann, distraught, circles round hiding the one she loves.
explanation.walkthrough: The jumbled pair of names splits in two, part before and part after the concealing word, which is why 'going round' is needed; love as O is the tennis score.
explanation.definitionFit: To be on a hiding to nothing is a British idiom for facing a contest one cannot win.

clue.text: Abstention called for in church. (Ales we mixed outside.)

indicators.note: outside says the scrambled letters sit around the other piece
mixed means stirred together, so these letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written, ready for scrambling
CH is the standard abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: Teetotalism is demanded in church, while the drinkers mix their ales outside.
explanation.definitionFit: Eschewal is the act of shunning or avoiding something, a deliberate abstention.

clue.text: Gathers the milk deliveryês finished?

parts.note: a milkman's delivery route is his round, and the possessive stands for 'is'
time is up when it is finished

explanation.surface: A question whether the milkman has completed his deliveries.
explanation.walkthrough: A milk round is the British daily delivery of milk to doorsteps; 'round's up' means the round is over.
explanation.definitionFit: To round up is to collect people or animals together into one place, so it gathers them.

clue.text: Shocks with a "tune" that's dissonant?

indicators.note: dissonant means clashing and out of harmony, so these letters are thrown out of order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A composer startles audiences with a so-called tune full of discord.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and a description of the composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Karlheinz Stockhausen was a German avant-garde composer whose electronic, atonal works shocked many listeners.

clue.text: In summer month girl has cut out middle growth that's excessive

indicators.note: in says one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: June is a summer month

indicators.note: removing the middle leaves only the two ends of the word

parts.note: the first and last letters only

explanation.surface: In midsummer, a girl has had her waist-length hair cut, as it had grown too long.
explanation.definitionFit: A jungle is dense, tangled vegetation, growth run riot.

clue.text: Stage unit in a circle?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a step or level in a process
second meaning: one of the 360 divisions of a full turn

explanation.walkthrough: 'Stage' and 'circle' suggest a theatre, with the dress circle; the two halves are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a step in a progression and a measure of angle, 360 to a full rotation.

clue.text: Cut end off pocket cloth to make loop

indicators.note: cutting the end off removes the final letter of the word

parts.note: a hanky is a handkerchief, carried in a pocket

explanation.surface: Trimming a handkerchief's edge to form a loop.
explanation.definitionFit: A hank is a coil or looped skein of yarn, rope or wire.

clue.text: Look certain after record brings revelation

indicators.note: after says the words before it are placed behind the word that follows it, so the record goes first

parts.note: a disc is a gramophone record
lo is an old word meaning look
sure means certain

explanation.surface: Checking the records produces a startling revelation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' places the first two pieces behind the record, so the clue's order is reshuffled.
explanation.definitionFit: A disclosure is the act of making something known, a revelation of facts.

clue.text: Examined closely, not like a paperback

definitions.meaning: first meaning: reconnoitred, as a burglar does a house

definitions.note: describes a book bound in hard covers
definitions.meaning: second meaning: bound in hard covers, as a hardback is

explanation.walkthrough: To case a joint is criminal slang for checking it out before a robbery.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both the past tense of a verb for scouting a place and an adjective for a book in a stiff binding.

clue.text: A language originally in holy setting

definitions.text: A language originally in holy setting

indicators.note: a setting surrounds what is placed in it, like a jewel in a mount

parts.note: pi is slang for pious
taken as written

indicators.note: originally means at the start, keeping just the opening letter

parts.note: the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A tongue first spoken in a sacred context.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer, since it is the language of the Theravada Buddhist scriptures; pi is British school slang for pious.
explanation.definitionFit: Pali is an ancient Indian language preserved as the scriptural tongue of Theravada Buddhism.

clue.text: Caribbean celebrity, ace surrounded by island plants

indicators.note: surrounded by means enclosed, so the single letter sits inside the next piece

parts.note: WI stands for the West Indies
a star is a celebrity
IS is the abbreviation for island
A is the abbreviation for ace in cards

explanation.surface: A Caribbean star and a top player are surrounded by island flora.
explanation.definitionFit: Wistarias, usually spelled wisterias, are climbing plants with hanging clusters of flowers.

clue.text: The Peaceful King raged uncharacteristically

indicators.note: acting out of character means behaving in an unusual way, so the letters take an unusual order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A king known for calm lost his temper, quite out of character.
explanation.walkthrough: The contrast between 'Peaceful' and 'raged' gives the surface its irony.
explanation.definitionFit: Edgar, king of England from 959 to 975, is known to history by the epithet the Peaceable.

clue.text: Bird making circuit, a flier

parts.note: a lap is one circuit of a track
a wing is the limb that flies, or an air force unit

explanation.surface: A bird flying a full circuit.
explanation.definitionFit: The lapwing is a crested plover of farmland and marsh, also called the peewit.

clue.text: Dick can no longer see, presumably

definitions.text: Dick can no longer see, presumably

parts.note: surface reading: a man called Dick has gone blind
setter's reading: a nickname for a crack shot, taken literally as an organ of sight that has died

explanation.walkthrough: The nickname of a famous Wild West marksman is read literally, as if his eye had stopped working.
explanation.definitionFit: A dead-eye is an expert marksman, from the legendary nickname paired with Dick.
